ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r2.claim: Re-creation is easy for the One who made the heavens and earth and arranged night, day, and human sustenance; power enables it and wisdom entails it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p150/r2.anchor: His power bears witness that He can do so and His wisdom entails that He should do so.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p163/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p163/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p163/r3.claim: The sky's complexity and providential order show God's power to recreate people and need to hold them accountable, answering denial and establishing Judgment's wisdom.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p163/r3.anchor: not only an answer has been given to the objection raised by the rejecters of the Day of Judgement

BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p308#s079/r1.claim: The surah’s purpose is to establish resurrection and the gathering, displaying humanity’s final fate after the preceding surahs’ full exposition; its oaths show the matter has reached its decisive climax.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r9.claim: The question about whether people or heaven is harder to create may address all people, especially unbelievers, or be a command to Muhammad to tell them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r9.anchor: ثم وقفهم مخاطبة منه تعالى للعالم والمقصد الكفار، ويحتمل أن يكون المعنى: قل لهم يا محمد أأنتم أشد خلقا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r10.claim: The verse shows that bodily resurrection is not beyond God's power.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r10.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل على أن بعث الأجساد من القبور لا يتعذر على قدرة الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r11.claim: سمك is the height between the heaven's lower surface facing us and its upper surface.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r11.anchor: و «السمك» : الارتفاع الذي بين سطح السماء الأسفل الذي يلينا وسطحها الأعلى الذي يلي ما فوقها

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r12.claim: فسواها may mean making heaven smooth and even or perfectly constructing it; God knows its exact nature.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p433#2/r12.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فسواها يحتمل أن يريد جعلها ملساء مستوية ليس فيها مرتفع ومنخفض

JISHUMI:v10p7275/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r11.claim: The creation of the heavens, earth, mountains, light, and darkness proves resurrection: if God can preserve created substances, He can restore and revive them after their destruction.
JISHUMI:v10p7275/r11.anchor: الآيات تدل على صحة البعث بما بين من خلق السماء، والأرض والجبال، والنور والظلمة

STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r8.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r8.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r8.claim: The wonders of creation are presented as evidence that God can resurrect.
STUDYQURAN:79:intro/r8.anchor: cite the wonders of creation as evidence of God’s ability to resurrect

TABATABAI:79:27-34/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r2.claim: The question whether humans or heaven are harder to create rebukes deniers and answers their doubt: God created what is greater and can recreate humans.
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r2.anchor: بأن الله خلق ما هو أشد منكم خلقا فهو على خلقكم وإنشائكم النشأة الأخرى لقدير

TABATABAI:79:27-34/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r3.claim: The cosmic order's connection to human life also argues for God's lordship, prophecy, obligations, and the resurrection where deeds are repaid, introducing 79:34 onward.

TABATABAI:79:27-34/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r4.claim: The question is a rebuke designed to remove the perceived difficulty of resurrection; “He built it” begins a detailed explanation of heaven's creation.
TABATABAI:79:27-34/r4.anchor: استفهام توبيخي بداعي رفع استبعادهم البعث بعد الموت

TABRISI:79:45/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:45/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:45/r11.claim: Samk means height, opposed to depth; the heavens are the elevated structures, as in Ali's phrase and al-Farazdaq's verse.
TABRISI:79:45/r11.anchor: السمك الارتفاع وهو مقابل العمق لأنه ذهاب الجسم بالتأليف إلى جهة العلو

TABRISI:79:27-46/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:27-46/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:27-46/r1.claim: Taswiya is making one thing equal in measure to another, either in itself or by judgment.
TABRISI:79:27-46/r1.anchor: والتسوية جعل أحد الشيئين على مقدار الآخر في نفسه أو في حكمه

TABRISI:79:27-46/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:27-46/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:27-46/r9.claim: The passage challenges resurrection deniers: recreating people after death is no harder for God than creating the sky.
TABRISI:79:27-46/r9.anchor: يعني أخلقكم بعد الموت أشد عندكم وفي تقديركم أم السماء

TABRISI:79:27-46/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:27-46/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:27-46/r10.claim: This argument echoes the assertion that creating the heavens and earth is greater than creating people.
TABRISI:79:27-46/r10.anchor: وهما في قدرة الله تعالى واحد وهذا كقوله

TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r1.claim: God built the sky, raised its roof, and made it smooth without cracks, fissures, or unevenness; another view says it was made fit for angels.
TABRISI:79:27-46#2/r1.anchor: { رفع سمكها } سقفها وما ارتفع منها { فسواها } بلا شقوق ولا فطور

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r1.claim: The challenge asks whether the deniers or the heavens are greater in creation.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:79:27-34/r1.anchor: { أأنتم } أيها المنكرون للبعث { أشد خلقا أم السماء بناها }

ELMALILI:79:6-26#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:6-26#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:6-26#3/r1.claim: After Moses' story, God rebukes deniers by showing His supreme lordship and power, the ease of creation and resurrection for Him, and the severity of the afterlife punishment for transgressors.
ELMALILI:79:6-26#3/r1.anchor: Bu kıssadan sonra Allah teâlâ’nın rubûbiyetinin, kudretinin yüksekliğini ve O’na nazaran halk ve ba‘sin kolaylığını ve azgınlar hakkında âhiret azâbının şiddetini anlatmak üzere münkirlere tevbih tarîkiyle buyuruluyor ki:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r8.claim: For deniers of resurrection, recreating people after death is no harder to God's power than creating the heaven; both are equal to Him, as 40:57 says.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p329/r8.anchor: أخلقكم بعد الموت أشد عندكم وفي تقديركم أم السماء؟ وهما في قدرة الله واحد

NAHHAS:v5p143/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p143/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p143/r17.claim: The creation of the sky is more difficult than your resurrection, so why deny resurrection?
NAHHAS:v5p143/r17.anchor: أي لم تنكرون البعث وخلق السماء أشد من بعثكم

SAMIN-DURR:79:27/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:27/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:27/r1.claim: أم السماء is conjoined to أنتم.
SAMIN-DURR:79:27/r1.anchor: قوله: { أم السمآء }: عطف على " أنتم "

SAMIN-DURR:79:27/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:79:27/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:79:27/r2.claim: بناها explains how the heaven was created, so the pause falls after السماء; the construction parallels 43:58.
SAMIN-DURR:79:27/r2.anchor: وقوله: " بناها " بيان لكيفية خلقه إياها. فالوقف على " السماء " ، والابتداء بما بعدها. ونظيره ما مر

ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n12/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n12/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n12/r1.claim: Here, heaven is a metonym for the cosmic system, as elsewhere in the Qur'an; Asad points to his note on 2:29.
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n12/r1.anchor: The "heaven" is here, as in many other places in the Qur'an, a metonym for "cosmic system"

ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n12/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n12/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n12/r2.claim: The passage echoes 40:56-57; Asad says both passages counter a man-centered universe by stressing humanity's smallness beside cosmic vastness and complexity.
ASAD-NOTES:79:27#n12/r2.anchor: Both these passages refute the "man-centred" view of the universe by pointing out man's insignificance as compared with the vastness and complexity

QIRAAT-ER:79:27:1#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:79:27:1#1/r1.speaker: HzT
QIRAAT-ER:79:27:1#1/r1.claim: The HzT performance variant eases or alters hamza at the opening ءَأَنتُمْ boundary without changing the pronoun, comparison, or word identity.
QIRAAT-ER:79:27:1#1/r1.anchor: Hamza-related performance eases or alters realization at the opening ءَأَنتُمْ boundary

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r1.claim: The oath’s answer addresses Meccan deniers of resurrection with a rebuke: is creating you again harder, in your estimation, than creating the immense, wondrous sky?
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r1.anchor: خطاب للمخاطبين في جواب القسم أعني لتبعثن من أهل مكة المنكرين للبعث بناء على صعوبته في زعمهم بطريق التوبيخ والتبكيت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r2.claim: Khalqan is an accusative of specification, transformed from the predicate position: ‘Is your creation after death harder?’
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r2.anchor: ونصب خلقا على التمييز وهو محول عن المبتدأ أي أخلقكم بعد موتكم أشد

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r3.claim: The comparison concerns the creation of the sky, whose vastness and intricate marvels confound minds even at their smallest detail.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r3.anchor: أم خلق السماء على عظمها وانطوائها على تعاجيب البدائع التي تحار العقول عن ملاحظة أدناها

ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r4.claim: The following description elaborates the creation of the sky; leaving the agent unstated in these verbs signals that God alone is self-evidently meant and magnifies His greatness.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p31#2/r4.anchor: وقوله تعالى بناها الخ بيان وتفصيل لكيفية خلقها المستفاد من قوله تعالى أم السماء وفي عدم ذكر الفاعل فيه وفيما عطف من الأفعال من التنبيه على تعيينه وتفخيم شأنه عز وجل

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r1.claim: Ashaddu khalqan means more difficult to create.

BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:79:27-31/r2.claim: After asking whether people or the heaven is harder to create, the passage explains the heaven's construction.

BINTSHATI:v1p150/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r1.speaker: أبو حيان
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r1.claim: Abu Hayyan identifies the people addressed as deniers of resurrection, who reject it because returning decayed humans to life seems impossible.
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r1.anchor: والمقصود منكرو البعث، على ماقال "أبو حيان"

BINTSHATI:v1p150/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r2.claim: The cosmic signs are framed as a question so deniers will answer themselves; reflection shows that recreating decayed bones is no harder than creating heaven.
BINTSHATI:v1p150/r2.anchor: وقد ساق القرآن هذه الآيات بأسلوب الاستفهام ليرجعوا إلى أنفسهم فيلتمسوا جواب ما سئلوا عنه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r6.claim: Pharaoh’s story culminates in proof of God’s total power, especially resurrection; denial of resurrection gathers evil, while belief gathers good, leading into the creation argument.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r6.anchor: وكان أعظم عبرتها القدرة التامة لا سيما على البعث كما هي مشيرة إليه بأولها وآخرها

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r7.claim: The direct plural question turns from the Prophet to all people because the proof is clear to everyone, while reproaching them with an appeal to their weakness.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r7.anchor: ملتفتا بعد تخصيص الخطاب به صلى الله عليه وسلم لما تقدم من دقة فهمه وجلالة علمه صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى عموم الخطاب لوضوح هذا البرهان لكل إنسان

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r8.claim: Humans are weak and the sky, with its immense size, height, and benefits, is plainly more difficult to create.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r8.anchor: أصعب وأثقل من جهة التقدير والإيجاد

BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r9.claim: God made the sky a roof over the earth; creating the greater sky proves His power to recreate lesser human beings.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p317/r9.anchor: جعلها سقفا للأرض على ما لها من العظمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r3.claim: The passage turns from threatening examples of past nations to answer the mockers’ claim that decayed bodies cannot return, stated in 79:10.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r3.anchor: انتقال من الاعتبار بأمثالهم من الأمم الذي هو تخويف وتهديد على تكذيبهم الرسول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r4.claim: The direct “you” addresses the polytheists, shifting from the earlier third-person report of what they say; it names the people whose objection is being answered.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r4.anchor: فلذلك قيل لهم هنا أأنتم بضميرهم ولم يقل : آالإنسان أشد خلقا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r5.claim: The confirmatory question forces them to concede that creating the heavens is greater than creating humankind; since God created heaven, He can recreate people, as 40:57 states.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r5.anchor: والمقصود من التقرير إلجاؤهم إلى الإقرار بأن خلق السماء أعظم من خلقهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r6.claim: Custom had clouded their reasoning: they treated the unfamiliar resurrection as impossible without recognizing that God’s creation of something greater already establishes its possibility.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p82/r6.anchor: أن نظرهم العقلي غيمت عليه العادة فجعلوا ما لم يألفوه محالا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r1.claim: Stopping at a Quranic sentence ending can be essential to the meaning, which may change with pause placement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r1.anchor: والوقف عند انتهاء جملة من جمل القرآن قد يكون أصلا لمعنى الكلام

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r11.claim: In 79:27, the verse ends at banaha and the pause falls after al-sama’; even when connected, syntax prevents banaha from being heard as part of the alternative to the question.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r11.anchor: وكذلك قوله تعالى ) أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء بناها (

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r13.claim: Because the Quran was revealed among Arabic speakers to be understood, its basic meanings were accessible to them; the challenge of inimitability concerns the special rhetorical abilities of their eloquent leaders.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r13.anchor: ولما كان القرآن مرادا منه فهم معانيه وإعجاز الجاحدين به وكان قد نزل بين أهل اللسان

IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r14.claim: Rhetorical embellishment is one source of inimitability; verse endings resemble poetic rhymes and rhymed prose cadences and are intentional in Quranic composition, so ignoring them neglects their purpose.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v1p82#2/r14.anchor: وكان من جملة طرق الإعجاز ما يرجع إلى محسنات الكلام من فن البديع ، ومن ذلك فواصل الآيات

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r1.claim: Addressing those who reject resurrection, the verse asks whether their creation or the heavens’ creation is greater.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r1.anchor: ثم خاطب منكري البعث فقال تعالى أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r2.speaker: بعض النحويين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r2.claim: Some grammarians, as al-Zajjaj reports, take banaha as an adjectival clause modifying al-sama: the heaven which He built.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج ذهب بعض النحويين إلى أن قوله تعالى بناها من صفة السماء فيكون المعنى أم السماء التي بناها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r3.speaker: قوم
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r3.claim: Another group says al-sama is not a relative construction; the sense is whether you or the heaven is greater in creation, after which He explains how He made it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r3.anchor: وقال قوم السماء ليس مما توصل ولكن المعنى أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء أشد خلقا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r4.speaker: المفسرون
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r4.claim: The commentators say people may regard their recreation after death or the making of heaven as more difficult, but both are equal in God’s power.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون أخلقكم بعد الموت أشد عندكم أم السماء في تقديركم وهما في قدرة الله واحد

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r5.claim: Banaaha means He raised it; anything elevated above something else is called a construction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p22#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى بناها رفعها وكل شيء ارتفع فوق شيء فهو بناء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r1.claim: The greater creation of the heavens argues that God can recreate people after their first creation.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r1.anchor: يعني: بل السماء أشد خلقا منكم،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r2.claim: Another verse says creating the heavens and earth is greater than creating people.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r2.anchor: كما قال تعالى: {لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r3.claim: The Quran asks whether the Creator of the heavens and earth can create people like them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r3.anchor: بقادر على أن يخلق مثلهم بلى وهو الخلاق العليم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r4.claim: God built the sky by raising it high, extending and leveling it, and adorning it with stars.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p316/r4.anchor: فقوله: {بناها} فسره بقوله: {رفع سمكها فسواها} أي: جعلها عالية البناء، بعيدة الفناء، مستوية الأرجاء، مكللة بالكواكب في الليلة الظلماء.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r1.claim: The question addresses deniers of resurrection: are you harder to create than the heaven?
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r1.anchor: الخطاب لمنكرى ا لبعث ، يعني { أءنتم } أصعب { خلقا } وإنشاء { أم السمآء }

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r2.claim: God built the heaven by raising its height to a vast expanse, described as a journey of five hundred years upward.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p697#2/r2.anchor: { رفع سمكها } أي جعل مقدار ذهابها في سمت العلو مديدا رفيعا مسيرة خمسمائة عام

MUQATIL:79:27-33/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r1.claim: God asks the Arabs whether they are stronger than the sky; since they are weaker, they should consider their own fate.
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r1.anchor: يقول: فما حالكم أنتم، يا بني آدم، وأنتم أضعف من السماء

MUQATIL:79:27-33/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:79:27-33/r2.claim: The sky's splitting in 82:1 and 84:1 underscores the force of the comparison.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r1.claim: The address is to people who deny resurrection.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r1.anchor: ﴿ أأنتم ﴾ يا منكرى البعث ﴿ أشد خلقا ﴾ أصعب خلقا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r2.claim: The predicate after al-samāʾ is omitted: the question means whether the sky is harder to create.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r2.anchor: مبتدأ محذوف الخبر أى أم السماء أشد خلقا ثم بين كيف خلقها

NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r3.claim: The omitted subject of built it is Allah; the next verse explains how He built the sky.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p315#5/r3.anchor: ثم بين كيف خلقها فقال ﴿ بناها ﴾ أى الله ثم بين البناء فقال

BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r1.claim: A Persian admonitory poem urges the hearer to turn from punishment toward pardon and leave heedlessness before shame arrives.
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r1.anchor: تويش ازعقوبت در عفو كوب كه سودى تدارد فغان زير وب

BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r2.claim: Addressing Meccan deniers, the rhetorical question challenges their claim that resurrection is difficult: creating the immense, wondrous sky is harder by their reckoning, so restoring people is within God’s power.
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r2.anchor: خطاب لأهل مكة المنكرين للبعث بناء على صعوبته في زعمهم بطريق التوبيخ والتبكيت

BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r3.claim: The comparison follows the statement that resurrection requires only one blast, underscoring its ease for God.

BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r4.claim: The question seeks their admission that the heavens are harder to create, forcing them to concede that the easier resurrection is possible.
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r4.anchor: وهو استفهام تقرير ليقروا بأن خلق السماء

BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r5.claim: Antum is the subject, ashadd its predicate, khalqan a specification, and al-samāʾ is coordinated with antum with its predicate elided.
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r5.anchor: قوله أأنتم مبتدأ وأشد خبره وخلقا تمييز والسماء عطف على أنتم وحذف خبره

BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r6.claim: Banāhā resumes the sentence and details how the sky was created; the clause can begin after a pause at al-samāʾ, with am as a connected alternative.
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r6.anchor: وهو استئناف وتفصيل لكيفية خلقها المستفاد من قوله أم السماء فيتم الكلام حينئذ

BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r7.claim: Calling the sky a building rather than a roof highlights its resistance to disorder and collapse, despite building usually naming lower structures.
BURSEVI:v10p251#2/r7.anchor: واستعمل البناء في موضع السقف فإن السماء سقف مرفوع والبناء إنما يستعمل في أسافل البناء

QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r1.claim: Addressing Meccans, the verse asks whether creating them after death is harder than creating heaven; the one able to create heaven can resurrect them.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r1.anchor: يريد أهل مكة، أي أخلقكم بعد الموت أشد في تقديركم

QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r2.claim: The question is a reproach and rebuke.

QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r3.claim: God built heaven by raising it above the people like a building.
QURTUBI-FULL:79:27-30/r3.anchor: ثم وصف السماء فقال: { بناها } أي رفعها فوقكم كالبناء.

RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r1.claim: Rāzī prefers an argument for resurrection: humans are small beside heaven, so recreating them after death is within God’s power; relative scale matters only in human estimation.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r1.anchor: والمعنى أخلقكم بعد الموت أشد أم خلق السماء أي عندكم

RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r2.claim: An alternative reads the comparison as proof that humans are created; Rāzī calls this weak because deniers of human creation could deny the heaven’s creation too, and the sūra began with resurrection.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r2.anchor: المقصود من هذا الاستدلال بيان كونهم مخلوقين

RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r3.speaker: الكسائي والفراء والزجاج
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r3.claim: Al-Kisāʾī, al-Farrāʾ, and al-Zajjāj take the sentence to end at “or the heaven,” making “He built it” a new sentence.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r3.anchor: قال الكسائي والفراء والزجاج : هذا الكلام تم

RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r4.speaker: أبو حاتم
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r4.claim: Abū Ḥātim pauses at “He built it” and connects the phrase to “the heaven,” with an omitted relative pronoun: “the heaven which He built.”
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r4.anchor: وعند أبي حاتم الوقف على قوله

RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r5.speaker: القفال
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r5.claim: Al-Qaffāl supports the omitted-relative reading with a valid Arabic example; otherwise “He built it” and “raised its height” would be successive unrelated adjectives needing a conjunction.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r5.anchor: قال القفال : يقال : الرجل جاءك عاقل

RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r6.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r6.claim: Al-Farrāʾ objects that the relative reading implies a heaven that God did not build, which is impossible.
RAZI-FULL:v31p40#4/r6.anchor: وللفراء أن يحتج على قوله بأنه لو كان قوله

RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r1.claim: Rāzī argues that heaven is a body and every body is originated: an eternal body would have to be either moving or at rest.
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r1.anchor: الجسم لو كان أزليا لكان في الأزل إما أن يكون

RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r2.claim: Eternal motion is impossible because motion means being preceded by another state, whereas eternity excludes any such precedence.

RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r3.claim: Rest is a positive state, since motion and rest differ only in prior occupancy; heaven moves now, so its rest is removable and contingent, requiring an agent.
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r3.anchor: السكون وصف ثبوتي وهو ممكن الزوال

RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r4.claim: A necessary cause or necessary condition would make rest endure, while a contingent cause leads to regress or a necessary endpoint; a free agent acts by intention, which cannot bring about an already existing state.
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r4.anchor: ذلك المؤثر لا بد وأن يكون فاعلا مختارا

RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r5.claim: Because a body cannot be eternal either in motion or rest, heaven is originated and needs a maker for its existence and arrangement; reason establishes that its builder is God.
RAZI-FULL:v31p41/r5.anchor: فثبت بالعقل أن باني السماء هو الله تعالى

RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r1.claim: The second proof says everything besides the Necessary Existent is possible, originated, and caused: two necessary beings would be composite and dependent, while a caused thing must originate.
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r1.anchor: كل ما سوى الواجب فهو ممكن وكل ممكن محدث وكل محدث فعل صانع

RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r2.claim: The third proof says heaven’s size could be a little larger or smaller; its exact measure therefore requires a determiner and builder.
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r2.anchor: صريح العقل يشهد بأن جرم السماء لا يمتنع أن يكون أكبر مما هو الآن

RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r3.speaker: سائل
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r3.claim: A proposed objection asks whether God might create a being with power to make bodies, so that this intermediary built heaven.
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r3.anchor: خلق شيئا وأعطاه قدرة يتمكن ذلك المخلوق بتلك القدرة

RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r4.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r4.claim: Some scholars say reason proves an originated heaven and an ultimate eternal God, while revelation establishes that God, rather than an intermediary, built it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r4.anchor: من العلماء من قال : المعلوم بالعقل أنه

RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r5.speaker: بعض العلماء
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r5.claim: Others argue reason excludes an intermediary: all possible things are equally within God’s power, and one effect cannot result from two independent agents.
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r5.anchor: ومنهم من قال بل العقل يدل على بطلانه لأنه لما ثبت أن كل ما عداه محدث ثبت أنه قادر لا موجب

RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r6.claim: Rāzī calls the second argument sound for those who hold that no effective agent exists besides the One.
RAZI-FULL:v31p42/r6.anchor: لكن على قول من لا يثبت في الوجود مؤثرا سوى الواحد

RAZI-FULL:v31p43/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p43/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p43/r1.claim: After stating that God built heaven, the passage turns to explain how He built it.
RAZI-FULL:v31p43/r1.anchor: واعلم أنه تعالى لما بين في السماء أنه بناها

RAZI-FULL:v31p45#4/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#4/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#4/r4.claim: Rāzī says the creation of heaven and earth establishes God’s ability to resurrect; after proving resurrection rationally, the passage announces that it will occur.
RAZI-FULL:v31p45#4/r4.anchor: ذكر كيفية خلقة السماء والأرض ليستدل بها على كونه قادرا على الحشر والنشر

STUDYQURAN:79:27/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:79:27/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:79:27/r1.claim: God's creation of the sky, which some opponents already accepted, is evidence that He can resurrect people as He wills; the verse links this argument to 40:57 and 36:81.
STUDYQURAN:79:27/r1.anchor: is here cited as evidence that God would have no problem resurrecting human beings as He wills

TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r1.claim: Addressing Quraysh's deniers of resurrection, God argues that the builder of heaven can easily recreate people; their resurrection is no harder than creating heaven.
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r1.anchor: وقوله: {رفع سمكها فسواها} [النازعات: 28] يقول تعالى ذكره

TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p88#2/r2.claim: Bana-ha here means that God raised the heaven and made it a roof for the earth.

THALABI:v10p127/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p127/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p127/r8.claim: Since God created the heaven, He can resurrect the dead; the source links this proof to the statement that creating the heavens and earth is greater than creating people.
THALABI:v10p127/r8.anchor: إن الذي قدر على خلق السماء قادر على أن يحيي الموتى وقوله لخلق السماوات والأرض أكبر من خلق الناس

THALABI:v10p127/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p127/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p127/r9.claim: Banaaha means that God raised the heaven's height as its roof.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191/r2.claim: After the lesson from Pharaoh, the discourse turns to address those who deny resurrection.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r1.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r1.claim: Muqatil says the comparison concerns resurrection after death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r1.anchor: قال مقاتل: يعني بعثا بعد الموت (¬6).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r2.claim: The question asks whether recreating you after death is harder, in your reckoning, than making heaven; both are equally easy for God, who can resurrect you.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r2.anchor: والمعنى: أخلقكم بعد الموت أشد أم السماء؟ أي عندكم وفي تقديركم، وهما عند الله واحد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r3.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi instead takes it to ask whose workmanship is more perfect, but the author says this is remote.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r3.anchor: وليس معنى الآية: أنتم أحكم صنعة أم السماء!، وهذا قول الكلبي (¬1)، وهو بعيد

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r4.speaker: الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r4.claim: Al-Kisaʾi places the pause at al-samāʾ, then begins a new statement with banāhā.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r4.anchor: قال الكسائي: "أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء"

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r5.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r5.claim: Al-Farra reads the question as addressed to the people of Mecca, then says God described heaven by saying He built it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r5.anchor: قال الفراء (¬4): أأنتم يا أهل مكة أشد خلقا أم السماء، ثم وصف السماء، فقال: بناها.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r6.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r6.claim: Al-Zajjaj expands the question as “or is heaven stronger in creation?”; the next words explain how it was made.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r6.anchor: وقال الزجاج: أأنتم أشد خلقا، أم السماء أشد خلقا، ثم بين كيف خلقها، فقال: بناها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r7.speaker: أبو حاتم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r7.claim: Abu Hatim pauses at banāhā, taking it as a relative clause connected to heaven; the author prefers pausing at al-samāʾ, since heaven is not a relative antecedent.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r7.anchor: وعند أبي حاتم الوقف على قوله: "بناها" (¬8)؛ لأنه قال: من صلة السماء. المعنى التي بناها

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r8.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r8.claim: The commentators gloss samk as heaven’s roof or ceiling.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p191#2/r9.claim: God fashioned heaven without cracks or fissures.

ELMALILI:79:27-33/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r1.claim: The challenge primarily concerns resurrection and a new creation after death, but is phrased broadly to cover creation in general: are humans or the encompassing heaven harder to create?
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r1.anchor: Burada asıl mâna ölümden sonra yeni bir hilkatle yaratılış üzerindedir. Fakat bir kübrâ hâlinda daha şümullü olmak üzere sual mutlak halk üzerinde îrâd olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:79:27-33/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r2.claim: Heaven is the more immense creation: humans are like a particle within it, yet God built it by joining diverse subtle and dense materials and celestial bodies into an ordered whole through various forces.
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r2.anchor: بَنَىٰهَا} o Allah onu binâ etti.

ELMALILI:79:27-33/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r3.claim: Building means joining separate components to one another so their combination forms a whole; heaven is such a constructed whole.
ELMALILI:79:27-33/r3.anchor: “Binâ” müteferrik eczâyı yekdiğerine zamm u rabt ile mecmû‘undan bir kül inşâ etmektir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.claim: The vast, complex, ordered cosmos is evidence to resurrection deniers that its creator can raise people again; another verse says creating heaven and earth is greater than creating humanity.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r1.anchor: böylesine geniş ve kompleks olan, düzenli ve uyumlu işleyen varlıklar dünyasını yaratan kudretin insanları da öldükten sonra tekrar diriltebileceğine işaret edilmiştir.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r2.claim: God's creation of the heavens without pillars is among the signs of His limitless power and ability to resurrect.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r3.claim: Making night pitch dark and day bright is among the signs of God's limitless power and ability to resurrect.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:79:27/r3.anchor: geceyi zifiri karanlık, gündüzü ise aydınlık kılması (Bakara 2/164; Nebe’ 78/10-11)

ITQAN:v3p72/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p72/r2.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
ITQAN:v3p72/r2.claim: Saʿid ibn Jubayr reports a questioner bringing Ibn Abbas apparent conflicts about polytheists’ denial, questioning in the afterlife, the creation sequence, and the wording “was Allah.”
ITQAN:v3p72/r2.anchor: قال عبد الرزاق في تفسيره أنبأنا معمر عن رجل عن المنهال بن عمرو عن سعيد بن جبير قال جاء رجل إلى ابن عباس

ITQAN:v3p73/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p73/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v3p73/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas’s answers show that these passages differ by circumstance or meaning rather than contradicting one another; each was revealed as intended.
ITQAN:v3p73/r1.anchor: فما اختلف عليك من القرآن فهو يشبه ما ذكرت لك وإن الله لم ينزل شيئا إلا وقد أصاب الذي أراد

ITQAN:v3p73/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p73/r5.speaker: الحاكم
ITQAN:v3p73/r5.claim: Al-Hakim transmitted the full Ibn Abbas report and authenticated it; Ibn Hajar says its original is also in an authenticated collection and groups its questions into four apparent discrepancies.
ITQAN:v3p73/r5.anchor: أخرجه بطوله الحاكم في المستدرك وصححه

FARRA:v3p232/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p232/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p232/r2.claim: The question addresses the people of Mecca; the passage then describes the construction of heaven.
FARRA:v3p232/r2.anchor: أهل مكة ثم وصف صفة السماء، فقال: بناها

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r3.claim: The earth was created first in two days; the heavens, then smoke, were made in two; afterward God spread and anchored the gathered earth and grew its plants in two, totaling six days.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p47/r3.anchor: فابتدأ الخلق للأرض على ما في الآي الأول في يومين، ثم خلق السموات وكانت دخانا في يومين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.speaker: قالوا
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.claim: They argue that Fussilat places the earth's creation before the heavens, whereas al-Naziat appears to place the heaven's construction before the earth's spreading.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p25/r5.anchor: وقال بعد ذلك: ثم استوى إلى السماء وهي دخان فقال لها وللأرض ائتيا طوعا أو كرها

ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r4.claim: Some grammarians attach banāhā to al-samāʾ as a relative clause: “or the one who built it.”
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r4.anchor: قال بعض النحويين: (بناها) من صلة السماء، المعنى أم التي بناها

ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r5.claim: Others say al-samāʾ does not take a relative clause here; the comparison is whether you or the sky is greater in creation.
ZAJJAJ:v5p280/r5.anchor: وقال قوم: السماء ليس مما يوصل، ولكن المعنى أأنتم أشد خلقا أم السماء أشد خلقا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r14.claim: The address is general in form but targets deniers of resurrection, confronting them with God’s power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r14.anchor: الخطاب الظاهر أنه عام، والمقصود الكفار منكر والبعث، وقفهم على قدرته تعالى

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r15.claim: The sky is harder to create, as its permanence and resistance to change show.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p399/r15.anchor: فالمسؤول عن هذا يجيب ولا بد السماء، لما يرى من ديمومة بقائها وعدم تأثيرها

DURR-FULL:v8p410/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses raising the sky’s height as building it.
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله: {رفع سمكها} قال: بناها

DURR-FULL:v8p410/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r7.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r7.claim: Mujahid says the sky was raised without pillars, night was darkened, daylight brought forth, and the earth spread out.
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r7.anchor: عن مجاهد رضي الله عنه في قوله: {رفع سمكها} قال: رفع بنيانها بغير عمد

DURR-FULL:v8p410/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r8.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r8.claim: Qatada says God raised the sky’s structure, darkened night, brought out daylight as light, spread the earth, and fixed mountains so it would not sway.
DURR-FULL:v8p410/r8.anchor: وأخرج عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر عن قتادة رضي الله عنه في قوله: {رفع سمكها} قال: رفع بنيانها
